title: Weekly pilot retrospective - Emberfield benchmark handoff
summary: Weekly POC sync to review lab benchmarks vs incumbent: Redwood shows better median token latency and similar throughput at quantized profiles; 95th percentile latency still close to incumbent under tail loads. Discussed routing, KV cache priming, and dedicated slot request. Agreed next steps: run 95th percentile focused load with real traffic traces, share full benchmark spreadsheet and security pack, schedule canary for dedicated slots, pricing follow-up.
next_steps: Redwood to share complete benchmark spreadsheet and raw p95 traces (Maya) - due 2026-04-09
Customer to provide 24h traffic trace and top-100 prompts (Lena) - due 2026-04-10
Schedule canary run on dedicated slot with 95th-tail profile (Ethan/Maya) - target week of 2026-04-13
Redwood to send security pack and SOC2 summary (Jordan) - due 2026-04-08
Follow-up pricing for reserved slots and overage model (Maya) - due 2026-04-12
action_items: Maya Patel: export and upload raw bench CSV + p95 latency histograms to shared folder (due 2026-04-09)
Ethan Cole: prepare canary run playbook and routing fallback config (due 2026-04-11)
Lena Torres: deliver 24h production-like trace and top prompt set (due 2026-04-10)
Jordan Kim: attach security_deck link and KMS integration notes (due 2026-04-08)
Carlos Ruiz: confirm VPC peering constraints and existing firewall rules (due 2026-04-13)
transcript:
00:00 Maya Patel: ok hey everyone thanks for carving out the time, we're gonna run through this week's bench ret— um, retrospective for the emberfield pilot. duration估 45 minutes ish, hopefully we can hit the action items.
00:12 Lena Torres: thanks Maya, really quick, we had a couple of infra fires this morning so apologies if I pop in and out. but excited to see numbers.
00:20 Ethan Cole: no worries lena, we have the latest run from this morning — ran head-to-head vs the incumbent using your sample top-100 prompts and the 2k sequence mix.
00:30 Dr. Mark Hsu: quick question before we start — did you use quantized weights for Redwood's run? we need to know if there's any accuracy delta we should expect.
00:38 Ethan Cole: yea so the primary runs used int8 quantization plus a mid-tier KV cache warm path. we also did a fp16 baseline run — accuracy delta on zero-shot was within noise for our eval set, we logged the exact differences in the sheet.
:00:48 Lena Torres: ok good to know. can you call out latency numbers top level?
01:02 Ethan Cole: median token latency for generation profiles was about 12ms per token on Redwood hosted config vs incumbent at 18ms — so roughly 33% median improvement. throughput (tokens/sec) under sustained 200 concurrent sessions matched incumbent within 5% on the default routing. however when we pushed tail loads the p95 went from 120ms incumbent to 140ms on Redwood in that specific synthetic spike test.
01:30 Carlos Ruiz: so p95 is worse? that's a concern for our latency SLOs, we often need p95 < 150ms.
01:40 Maya Patel: totally fair, and we dug into that — two contributors: cold KV cache during the synthetic spike and queueing on the batching window when many short sessions align. we have mitigations: cache priming and dynamic batch window shrink on tail.
01:58 Jordan Kim: also routing; in that run we routed everything to a single high-throughput pool to compare unit cost. if we split by latency-critical routes into dedicated low-queue pools p95 improves ~20-30% in our microtests.
02:12 Nina Park: from procurement perspective we need a predictable number for reserved slots and an uplift for dedicated low-latency lanes. can you give a rough uplift number?
02:20 Maya Patel: yes rough sketches: dedicated low-latency pool is typically 1.4-1.7x base unit cost depending on GPU type and locality. we'll produce a formal pricing note once we know slot size.
02:33 Dr. Mark Hsu: about accuracy: were there any hallucination regressions at higher quant? send the eval diffs.
02:40 Ethan Cole: will do — we have side-by-side ROUGE/BLEU-ish metrics and a small human eval for critical prompts. no systematic hallucination spike observed, but a couple edge cases on long context where token truncation changed scoring — logged in the spreadsheet.
03:05 Lena Torres: can you share the sheet now?
03:10 Maya Patel: yes link in the chat — Spreadsheet: https://redwood.link/emberfield-bench — it has raw CSVs, histograms, and the test harness config at the bottom.
03:18 Carlos Ruiz: seeing the harness config, curious about the network emulation. did you replay real traffic or synthetic poisson bursts?
03:27 Ethan Cole: this round used your supplied trace replay for the main runs, plus synthetic bursts to characterize tails. the p95 weirdness showed up mainly in the synthetic burst profile where many short sessions align; when we replayed your 24h trace the p95 delta narrowed to ~10ms.
03:45 Lena Torres: that is more reassuring. the synthetic spikes are useful but our real-world traces are the truth for us.
03:50 Maya Patel: yes agreed. next test we propose: run a tail-focused replay using your 24h trace but with a canary that forces routing to a dedicated low-latency pool for 10% of traffic. that should isolate the tail behavior.
04:12 Nina Park: on security we need to know encryption at rest and KMS flow for private deploy — can you send SOC2 and KMS docs?
04:20 Jordan Kim: absolutely — sending Security deck link in chat: https://redwood.link/security-deck . we support customer-managed keys, HSM integrations, SSO via SAML, and audit logs. we also have per-route request logs for the private control plane.
04:38 Carlos Ruiz: about VPC peering — how does Redwood handle firewall rules inbound? do we need VPN or peering support?
04:45 Jordan Kim: both supported — we can do VPC peering or a managed transit gateway. for fully air-gapped we also have an on-prem package but that's a next step. I'll attach network topology notes.
05:00 Dr. Mark Hsu: curious re: caching — you mentioned KV cache priming, can you explain behavior on long-running chat sessions?
05:10 Ethan Cole: yes, we keep per-session KV cache on GPU memory keyed by session id; when traffic is sticky we hit warm cache and see sub-10ms incremental tokens. cold sessions pay the warm-up cost which is where the synthetic spikes hammer us. priming approaches: either pre-warm top-N sessions, or send a fast prefix-only warm request to prime the KV.
05:34 Lena Torres: how noisy are those warm-up operations on throughput? will priming add extra cost?
05:40 Ethan Cole: small extra cost — typically one small prefix request per session. but if you have millions of sessions it's non-trivial; we can optimize by priming only high-QPS session keys.
05:52 Maya Patel: circling back to routing — there's also an autosplit rule we can recommend: route by intent/latency tag so latency-critical flows always hit dedicated lanes, cheaper flows go to shared pools. reduces p95 without raising overall cost too much.
06:10 Lena Torres: that seems reasonable. for the head-to-head we should see the canary result with our traffic trace before we make a decision.
06:20 Maya Patel: yes. timeline wise — can we agree Lena will share the 24h trace by Friday?
06:25 Lena Torres: yes, I'll have procurement sign-off and deliver a scrubbed trace by 2026-04-10.
06:32 Nina Park: on procurement, we also need to see SLA language and data residency options.
06:36 Maya Patel: we'll include a draft SLA and residency options in the package Jordan will send with the security docs.
06:42 Carlos Ruiz: two quick technical asks: 1) can you provide p95 broken down by operation (generation vs embeddings) and by seq length? 2) can you surface CPU vs GPU time in the histograms?
06:55 Ethan Cole: yes to both — our harness logs op-level breakdown and CPU/GPU segmentation. will include in CSVs.
07:05 Dr. Mark Hsu: on quantization: if we push to int4 for cost reasons, do you have fallback to higher precision on a per-call basis?
07:12 Jordan Kim: we support model variants and dynamic fallback. calls can specify preferred precision and a fallback route on quality loss. we can wire that into your canary policy.
07:25 Lena Torres: good. back to pricing — Maya you said 1.4-1.7x for dedicated low-latency? can you give an example with numbers so procurement can evaluate?
07:34 Maya Patel: sure, rough example in the pricing note we'll send: base unit $X per GPU-hour — dedicated low-latency lane for a 4-GPU slice is ~1.5x effective unit. we'll convert to monthly reserved slot numbers in the note and show cost per 1M tokens for typical prompt mixes.
07:50 Nina Park: please make that as concrete as possible. we need a cost per 1M tokens and p95 SLA tradeoff matrix.
07:58 Maya Patel: noted. action items captured.
08:02 Lena Torres: small nit — we had a mismatch in labels in the sheet where some runs labeled 'incumbent' were actually our old config. please double-check the CSV labels before sharing.
08:12 Ethan Cole: good catch — will reconcile, thanks.
08:17 Maya Patel: ok last things — schedule: we'll run the dedicated-lane canary target week of 2026-04-13 once we have your trace and we've agreed slot size. Jordan will drop security pack by 2026-04-08. Maya will follow with pricing and the bench CSVs by 2026-04-09.
08:40 Dr. Mark Hsu: sounds fine. any blockers from Redwood side?
08:45 Maya Patel: none; biggest dependency is the anonymized 24h trace and confirmation on the slot capacity you want.
08:55 Carlos Ruiz: I'll review network constraints and get back by the 13th.
09:00 Maya Patel: excellent. thanks everyone. we'll send notes and action items in the thread.
09:06 Lena Torres: thanks all, good session.
09:10 [Call ends]
questions: What caused the p95 regression under synthetic tail loads?
Will quantization at int8/4 introduce hallucination regressions?
Can Redwood provide per-op p95 and CPU/GPU breakdowns?
What pricing uplift for dedicated low-latency lanes?
